items.title: A subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z on an irreducible space is a constant multiple on a nonempty open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: On an irreducible topological space X, the lemma shows that any abelian subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z agrees on some nonempty open with the constant sheaf of multiples of a fixed integer (statement lines 3634-3642). The proof uses that the constant sheaf has value Z on every nonempty open, disposes of the zero subsheaf, and then runs a descending induction on the positive generator n of the group of sections over a nonempty open on which the subsheaf is nonzero: if the inclusion of the constant multiples of n is strict, one can shrink and produce a strictly smaller positive integer, and the process must stop (proof lines 3644-3662). The claim is H2: one point of the definition of the constant sheaf on an irreducible space plus a well-founded descent on positive integers, with the shrinking step written out.
